important_discoveries: Audit (2026-09-26) verdict C; the 20 findings are AUD-01..AUD-20 on CRITICAL_FIXES, each linked to fix tasks.
Tracker formulas are verified by tools/tracker/excel_recalc.py against values computed from MASTER, not only for errors.
Repository fixtures are python-docx generated; Word-authored fixtures (audit a01-a12, r01-r05) are outside the repo (TEST-020).
scripts/e2e_server.py leaves %TEMP%/smartdoc-e2e-* dirs (TEST-006).
Docker daemon is not running on this machine; image builds are unverified locally (INFRA-010).
Excel/Word on this machine stamp MSIP_Label_* (tenant SiteId) into Office files on save; tracker.py and excel_recalc.py strip them, the pre-push scan flags them.
Editor schema (probe via getSchema(editorExtensions)): attribute-level drops remain for pasted textAlign, image width/height, link title, cell align/colwidth -> EDIT-008..011.
PDF export: a page break inside a table cell cannot be honoured (dropped there) - to report via FID-003.

Content check calibration on 17 Word-authored + 12 golden fixtures: all verified except a03 (heading numbers baked into text - genuine, AUD-04); a05 header variants lost is reported via header/footer check.
The browser preview tool is bound to the session's original folder (Claude - SGD): its .claude/launch.json got smartdoc-*-throwaway entries (untracked there).
One E2E run pasted at the document start (caret not yet placed by an early click); the test now checks focus and uses Ctrl+End.

Export read-back calibration: DOCX exports hold exactly the document's words on all 29 fixtures; PDF exports on all but a11-multilingual (Arabic unshaped/reversed, CJK and Devanagari missing - AUD-17), now reported at every export.

Section break type (w:type) belongs to the section it starts (ECMA-376 17.6.22): the importer used the ending section's type, so continuous breaks became page breaks - fixed, pinned by test_docx_detect.
Golden JSON export was non-deterministic (random uuids/timestamps): every regeneration rewrote all fixtures; now uuid5-by-order + fixed times.
Pasting into an empty paragraph poured the first pasted paragraph into it and dropped its attributes (ProseMirror fit) - fixed by pasteIntoEmptyBlock.ts.
Rule values were written into CSS unchecked (element style, page settings, AI instructions): SEC-022, fixed with formatting/values.py.
AppliedStyle's style attr is copied on split (a paragraph after a heading looked like the heading until reload): the editor now re-syncs block styles after each save.
Opening a document caused a save when a run had several marks: the editor lists marks in its schema order. Fixed with one canonical order (EDIT-007).
Pasted Markdown pictures (and their descriptions) vanished while the content check said verified: now named as left out (FID-006).
The old AI structure check (bag of words, 20% unknown allowed) passed sentence deletions, 'not' removal and 5->50 (AUD-02); replaced by text_check.check_text.
apply_formatting rebuilt the rules after instruction operations and dropped a style set on one element ('Applied 1 change', nothing changed); operations now apply after it.
The E2E server has a scripted AI (scripts/e2e_ai.py) answering two fixed instructions; everything else behaves as if no key.
A structure answer could store any documentType string, heading level 99 or a code language with quotes; AI answer fields are now bounded in ai/schemas.py (the SDK validates locally).
Word exports of imported documents are now written into the original package (only the body regenerated); the import report and capability matrix say what that keeps.
python-docx's add_comment references an undefined CommentReference style; exports now define the comment styles (found by the new package check).

A block's look is part of its fingerprint: a template restyles every block, so after one only page breaks (and the sections they carry) are copied; fields and content controls then rely on the kept-fragment path or are reported lost at import.

python-docx's add_section puts the section break on a new empty paragraph, owned by the page break the importer derives; Word may put it on the text paragraph itself (then an edit loses the section, and the export says so).
The earlier package check never exercised the copy path (golden documents were parsed, not stamped); test_original_blocks now stamps and exports all 13.
Word's default paragraph style applies to paragraphs without a pStyle; the detector now resolves it too (it used only docDefaults), so the report and the importer agree.
A paragraph style's bold/italic/underline used to be the block's look even when a run turned it off (the run showed it anyway); now the look drops it and the other runs carry marks.
python-docx's _apply_text_style appended w:highlight/w:shd at the end of rPr (out of schema order when an underline was set first); _put_in_rpr inserts in order.
ReportLab 5 draws <u kind='double'> and <u width='..'>, and <super|sub size rise> for raised or lowered text; it has no letter spacing and no dotted, dashed or wavy lines.

Word marks the language on runs; with an en-US default, Bulgarian runs carry bg-BG. A block written anew without it gets checked as English in Word, so language is modelled (textStyle.lang), not just reported.
Per ECMA-376, widow control is off unless a style turns it on; an explicit off against an unset base is no change (no rule), which the importer follows.

Section breaks are elements (not per-element section membership): the element list stays flat, the editor shows and moves them like page breaks, and each carries the settings of the section it ends -- as Word stores them.

Fingerprints (provenance.py) counted default values, so each field added to the model shifted every stored block's fingerprint (DOCX-017 tables, DOCX-018 flips): stored documents' blocks looked changed and were rewritten. Now defaults are left out; older stamps are checked by epoch (_STAMPED_BEFORE).

PDF: blocks nested in cells, list items and quotes had no style (only top-level elements get styleRef): Helvetica with leading = font size. Now they take the container's text look (_inside), as the editor does by CSS inheritance.

Word styles left properties unset (no w:b, no spacing, no indent) and the importer wrote no rule for them, so the render spec's defaults (bold headings, 8 pt spacing, 1 cm quote indent, italic captions, table gaps) stood in for Word's own implicit values (FMT-004). Imported styles are now completed with what Word draws (as_word_draws).

Word on this machine stamps identifying data into files it saves: Office sensitivity labels (MSIP_Label_* with the organisation's tenant) into docProps/custom.xml, and for comments the signed-in account's identity (w15:presenceInfo, an e-mail) into word/people.xml. make_word_fixtures.py scrubs both; test_word_fixtures.py guards the committed files.

The true fidelity test found: a Word export overwrote the file's title with the display title (first heading / filename); and the app resolved each kind fully at import, so a template changing Normal left lists/tables/captions/quotes/headings 4-6 in their imported look here while Word (styles based on Normal) gave them the new body look. Fixed: SourceProperties.title/importedTitle; inherit_from_normal on import; all styles written on export once Normal changes.

A SmartArt's cached drawing part is referenced only from its data part (dsp:dataModelExt relId, not an r: attribute), so the unused-relationship cleanup dropped it from every Word export into the original, copied blocks included; and Word itself writes r:blip="" in SmartArt layouts (not a missing relationship).

The fragment writer (_add_inline_runs_keeping) wrote a run of text only where one started at a fragment's edge: text in other formatting between two edges was silently left out of a paragraph written anew (pre-existing since the preservation layer; found by the true fidelity test on a06's bibliography).

P0 (pre-existing since DOCX-028): a block deleted in the editor comes back in a Word export into the original -- the copy plan takes an original child no element holds for one the import left out and copies it with the group before; a paragraph+picture group is copied after its picture is deleted. DOCX-028B.

Word ignores a reply's thread (commentsExtended paraIdParent) when the reply's commentReference comes before its parent's in the body; python-docx's add_comment puts a later comment's end and reference on the same run before an earlier one's (DOCX-021, _after_earlier_ends).
Word's Revisions.AcceptAll/RejectAll need a document window: open the document with Visible=True inside the hidden Word application (scratchpad/word_revisions.py).

A kept fragment whose text was edited is dropped by _place_fragments; for content controls (filled in by design) the import also keeps the text just before and after, and the export places the control between them (_between).

python-docx's styles[name] is case-sensitive beyond its own aliases: 'Footnote Text' misses Word's 'footnote text', and the exporter used to add a second style with the same id (FootnoteText). _named_style finds styles in any case; package_check names duplicate style ids.

The React compiler lint rule rejects passing a ref-reading function to an extension during render; a Tiptap extension's document-level input goes in its storage, set from an effect (setHeadingNumbering).

Kept fragments over the same text must nest: a control or link outermost, and the one opened last closes first -- a06's citation control around its CITATION field was written with the field crossing the control, a file Word calls corrupted (found by the Phase 3 gate, not by the package check, which now names it).

python-docx reads a DTD's entities as nothing (resolve_entities=False): a Word file with a DTD imported as an empty document without a word. And parts nothing reads (theme, font table, customXml) went in broken. Both refused now: every XML part is checked (well-formed, no DTD) before the file is opened.

pypdf mends a damaged PDF silently: a stream that doesn't decode or a missing object loses that text with only a logging warning. And text XML can't hold (a PDF's backspace, pasted control codes) was stored and then broke every Word export of the document. Both closed (SEC-011, SEC-023).
Under pytest 9, caplog's handlers are attached to non-propagating loggers too (pypdf's): check what reaches the root logger with a handler of your own, not caplog.

A warnings filter set at import time is lost when the import happens inside warnings.catch_warnings() (pytest's collection does that): security must not rest on one. Pillow's MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS (hard error past 2x) does not depend on filters.

The editor's autosave re-sent a failing save every 1.2 s: reconcile gives an unsaved block a fresh id per try, and the id sync fired an editor update that scheduled the next save. Its own writes are tagged and schedule nothing now.

preservedAttributes comes back from the browser as sent (keep_provenance restores only sourceBlocks/sourceHash) and _valid_fragment checks a field's instruction only for length: a crafted save can put any Word field (DDE, INCLUDEPICTURE) into the next Word export -- SEC-015.

python-docx keeps a part's relationships on save even when nothing refers to them any more: an unsafe link's relationship in a kept original travelled out in every Word export. The kept original is cleaned at upload now (SEC-016).

A Word SVG picture (svgBlip) is read as the PNG copy Word keeps with it: copied unchanged into the original it stays SVG, written anew it is the PNG, and no report says so (Phase 4 gate, a04; DOCX-018C).

A save's server cost stays in step with the document after PERF-003: the stored document is loaded and validated whole, dumped four times and written whole on every save (0.37 s at 1,651 elements, 2 s at 12,201), blocking the event loop meanwhile (PERF-008).

SQLite can't wait for its write lock in a transaction that has already read (it answers 'database is locked' to avoid a deadlock), so a lock taken after reads only serialises on PostgreSQL; the PLAN-003 race test sets the waiting transaction up to take the hold first.

Python's email package sends a body with long lines as quoted-printable, which turns '=' into '=3D' in the raw message: the development outbox writes 8-bit text so a file shows its links unbroken (SMTP keeps the standard encoding).
